note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0% (from 1.6%), 2026 lifted to 1.2%; gilt 10Y -2bp to 5.323%, sterling $1.3298 — the 'boring budget' bond markets wanted (Reuters/XTB). France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, neg outlook); OAT-Bund ~6bp wider on the week as France contracted (-0.1% Q3) and protests resume Saturday; revenue-section vote Nov 3; S&P reviews France Nov 27. ECB Oct 29: Lagarde steps down Feb 7, 2027 — succession starts immediately. No US shutdown — CR through Dec 11.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US Q3 GDP advance BEAT: 3.4% SAAR (vs 3.2% consensus, prev 2.2%); claims 194K (vs ~199K) — low-hire, low-fire intact. Fri morning: EZ Q3 GDP BEAT (+0.4% q/q vs 0.2% fcst, Ireland-flattered) but France CONTRACTED (-0.1% vs +0.1% exp) and Italy flat (0.0% vs +0.1%); German GDP BEAT (+0.2% vs +0.1%); EZ jobless up to 6.5% (vs 6.4%). Overnight: Tokyo CPI in line (core 2.6%), Japan IP BEAT (+2.2% m/m vs +1.3% exp) but retail MISSED (+2.3% y/y vs 3.3% exp), jobs tightened to 2.4%; Australia PPI a touch hot (+1.1% q/q vs 1.0% exp) into the RBA. 7:30am CT: US ECI INLINE (+0.8% q/q as expected, wages +0.7%, benefits +0.9%); Canada Aug GDP MISSED (flat 0.0% vs +0.2% exp) — loonie firmer anyway (USD/CAD ~1.3959) on the oil bid. Oct 30 US session: Chicago PMI MISSED at 55.3 (prev 58.8, WSJ poll 56.0) — cooling but still expanding; prices paid highest since Dec 2021. Weekend: China official PMIs MISSED Saturday (mfg 49.3 vs 50.0 poll, back in contraction; non-mfg 49.7) — RatingDog private read due Monday 8:45pm CT, then ISM manufacturing Monday 9:00am CT (fcst 54.5, prev 54.5).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US Sep PCE in line: headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y. AU Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's path: trimmed +1.0% q/q (Bank forecast 0.8%), Q3 trimmed 3.7% y/y, monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y (vs 4.2% exp) — Nov hike case firms; Q3 PPI +1.1% q/q adds pipeline heat. Tokyo CPI Oct: core in line at 2.6% y/y (headline 2.8%). Fri flash batch: French CPI HOT (3.4% y/y vs 3.2% exp, HICP 3.8%), Italian CPI a sharp beat (+5.4% y/y vs ~4.6% consensus), Spanish CPI inline at 4.9%; German flash CPI COOLED to 2.8% y/y (HICP 2.8% vs 3.1% poll, core 2.1%); EZ-wide flash CPI due Nov 4, not Oct 30 (calendar corrected Oct 30 evening). US CPI 3.7%, import prices +8.1% y/y; BoJ trend index 3.2% y/y in Sep (3-yr high, Reuters Oct 27) cements the Dec BoJ case. BoC MPR: Canada inflation 3.5% by end-2026, 3.1% in 2027, back to 2% only by mid-2028. US ECI Q3 INLINE: +0.8% q/q (wages +0.7%, benefits +0.9%) — labor costs cooling, not re-accelerating.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC HELD Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike) — December hike ~70% into the Oct 30 NY close (Prime Terminal via FXStreet, from 84% after the Oct 28 meeting). ECB HELD Oct 29 at 2.50% — Lagarde: direction of travel 'clear', a hike was debated; Reuters sources call a Dec 17 hike 'all but certain'; Lagarde steps down Feb 7, 2027. BoJ HELD Oct 30 at 1.25% (8-1, Takata for 1.50%) — Outlook Report calls underlying inflation 'generally consistent' with the 2% target, the first such call since 2013; Ueda vigilant on overshoot risk; December hike ~80%. BoC HIKED Oct 28 to 2.50% (first since July 2023); December further hike ~45%. RBA Nov 2-3 (hike ~79-85%), BoE Nov 5 (hike ~94%). RBNZ's Oct 28 surprise hold (4-3, 2.75%) delays tightening to Dec 9, not abandoning it. Oct 30 US session: Musalem wants a hike 'again soon', Logan 'at least two more' 25bp hikes then a pause — but Dec pricing trimmed to ~70% (Prime Terminal via FXStreet) from 84% post-meeting, as the tech sell-off pulled yields lower.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): specs extreme — euro net short at a 3-yr low, yen longs at the 98th percentile, AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes, GBP shorts at the 5th percentile; crowded shorts are squeeze fuel if the data turns. Overnight: AI-led risk-off knocked DXY below 102.00 as the yen held into the BoJ; oil jumped (Brent ~$116.1, WTI ~$103.4, intraday $106.2 — highest since mid-Sep) on reports of possible renewed US action on Iran — WSJ: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper briefed Trump on options Thu; strikes possible after the Nov 3 midterms; a tanker was struck near Hormuz Thu (UKMTO). Houthi claims on Saudi refineries continue; Vance's letter earlier sought to revive Iran talks. Gold slipped below $4,000. The haven bid is split this time — yen and franc firmer, dollar softer. US session: gold crashed below $3,900 (-3%+, a one-year low) even as the dollar softened and yields fell — liquidation, not a dollar story; tech sell-off day two.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent Dec ~$116.57 (+0.7%) / WTI ~$104.15 (+2.1%) at the NY close (Finnhub/OANDA + Edge wrap Oct 30) — up on Iran-strike reports; Brent Dec contract expired today, Jan ~$112; spread ~$12.40. EIA drew -1.9M bbl to 410.6M bbl (week ended Oct 23). Net importers (EUR/JPY) still pay the tax; exporters (AUD/CAD) get the tailwind.
tot.title: Terms of trade
